QF.id: IV Fixed Income Instruments and Bond Markets_6

question.text: A bond has a Macaulay duration of 7.50 years and a yield to maturity of 6%. What is its Modified Duration?

explanation.text: The Logic: Modified Duration = Macaulay Duration / (1 + YTM/k), where k is the number of coupon periods per year. For an annual-coupon bond, 7.50 / 1.06 = 7.075, which rounds to 7.08 years. The Trap: 7.50 is the Macaulay duration itself. 7.28 results from using YTM/2 in the denominator, which is the convention for semi-annual coupon bonds, not annual. Note: The workbook illustrates the annual-versus-semi-annual denominator distinction directly in the same chapter.
